question: build the probe-scroll precondition as a reusable gate, and prove it discriminates on the known positives and the known negatives

gate.principle: it does not know which open path ran; it asks whether any scrollable container ended the cell away from its natural origin, and says how far and how far it could have gone
gate.falsifiedByItsOwnFirstRun: the verdict enum was designed to separate 651's class from 652's, and it does not: within 651's single path, whether the scroll reached the end depends on the viewport height. The stable discriminator is 652's — does the offset DRIFT with the viewport — not whether it reached the end.

detail.why: 651 proved @fov-hover@ scrolls and drifts; 652 proved camera-preset-panel scrolls but holds 12/19. A gate that stayed quiet on either would be broken; a gate that fired on the other nine would be noise.

the-gate-fires-on-exactly-the-two-known-.note: a gate that cannot fail is not a gate — this is the positive set

the-gate-is-silent-on-all-nine-known-neg.note: and a gate that fires on everything is not a gate either

the-gate-fires-at-every-viewport-height-.note: a gate sampled at one viewport would have passed at 1440x900 and missed 651 entirely

detail.whatTheFirstRunGotWrong: it assumed 'reached the end' is a property of the PATH. It is a property of the path AND the viewport: 654 read 'scrolled-to-end' at 1150 and 'partial-scroll' at 720 for the same path, and 651's file says the same thing (374 of 374 vs 779 of 804). A binary reached-the-end gate would have passed 3 of 651's 6 heights and missed the retraction on the other 3.
detail.theCorrection: drift, not end-reached. 652's criterion is the stable one and 654 keeps it.

the-stable-discriminator-is-drift-not-th.note: a check that fails because its premise was wrong is worth more than one that passed because the premise happened to hold

detail.comparedAgainst: batch651 runtime-audit.json hoverMode.*.locate, read from the file (not retyped)
detail.why: 651's numbers came from a probe whose whole point is that it misleads. Citing them would be circular. 654 runs its own six heights and compares.

the-project-open-path-denominator-is-now.note: every one of these sites is a place a future reading could be contaminated and not know it. A file that failed to parse would make the denominator quietly short, so it is a failure here rather than a silent skip.

detail.howToReadThis: 15 paths have been measured against the gate; the denominator is ~4 orders of magnitude larger. That gap is the honest state of this project, stated as a number so it can only shrink.
detail.note: not a pass/fail on the gap — a pass/fail would be either vacuous or unachievable. It is a ratchet.

the-measured-set-is-a-documented-fractio.note: the gap is recorded, not asserted away

detail.why: 651 found hover() can throw while the overlay is mounted. A cell whose open threw still gets a gate reading, so a throw must not be read as 'clean' — the two facts are reported separately.

detail.theDraftActuallyCounted: the number of verifier files that contain at least one
detail.theSelfReference: at the time the draft was written, the file doing the counting was itself one of the 259, because it quoted the number in its own docstring
detail.whyItWentUnnoticed: 258 is neither zero nor absurd. It looks like a census. Only measuring it twice, with two methods, showed it.

the-draft-denominator-was-a-file-count-n.note: the denominator was wrong before anyone relied on it — and the fix is not 'write it more carefully', it is 'make it a live read that changes when the project changes'
